root_cause.text: f2fs_fill_super() fails to handle the positive return value from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() when the mount is read-only, causing a non-zero positive error code to be returned to vfs_get_tree() which triggers a kernel BUG at fs/super.c:1761.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the error handling in f2fs_fill_super() to check if err > 0 regardless of read-only state; previously the condition `if (!f2fs_readonly(sb) && err > 0)` only handled the read-write case, leaving the read-only path to propagate a positive err. The commit message explicitly states: "The root cause is we missed to handle error number returned from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() when mounting image w/ ro,norecovery or ro,disable_roll_forward mount option, result in returning a positive error number to vfs_get_tree()."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix readonly mount by resetting err to 0 when fsync recovery returns pending data, instead of leaving a positive err that could cause unexpected failures.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition after f2fs_recover_fsync_data from a single if with && to a nested if-else. The outer condition checks if err > 0; inside, if the filesystem is not readonly, the original error handling (set err to -EINVAL, log error, goto free_meta) is performed; if readonly, err is reset to 0 and an info message is logged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when f2fs_recover_fsync_data returns a positive value (indicating pending fsync data), the code now distinguishes between read-write and readonly mounts. For read-write, it still fails with -EINVAL. For readonly, it clears the error and allows the mount to proceed, effectively dropping the unrecoverable fsync data.

grouping_result.intent: Fix readonly mount by resetting err to 0 when fsync recovery returns pending data, instead of leaving a positive err that could cause unexpected failures.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by handling the positive return value from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() on a read-only mount, resetting err to 0 to prevent the non-zero positive error code from propagating and triggering a kernel BUG.

candidates.rationale: This assignment stores the return value of f2fs_recover_fsync_data(), which can be a positive number indicating pending fsync data. When the mount is read-only, this positive value is not reset to 0, causing a non-zero positive error code to propagate and trigger a kernel BUG.

This conditional only handles the positive err when the mount is not read-only. It fails to account for the read-only case, leaving err positive. The fix requires resetting err to 0 for read-only mounts to prevent the positive error from being returned to vfs_get_tree().

vuln_statements.explanation: This assignment stores the return value of f2fs_recover_fsync_data() into err. When the mount is read-only, this value can be positive (indicating pending fsync data), and the subsequent code fails to reset err to 0 for the read-only case, causing a non-zero positive error code to propagate to vfs_get_tree() and trigger a kernel BUG.

This conditional only handles the positive err value when the mount is not read-only. It fails to account for the read-only case, leaving err positive and causing the vulnerable propagation of a non-zero error code.
